answer: A practical sybil defence is to make identity expensive to forge yet cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a small refundable stake and build a public history of completed work, like a trellis that only grows one verified rung at a time. New identities start with narrow permissions and a short horizon for rewards, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more than any payout they could harvest, while honest agents gradually earn broader access through consistent, checkable behaviour.
